outcomes.original: Filing step: Request a written zoning determination from SF Planning Department on whether a 24,138 square-foot bar use can be authorized in NCD-CASTRO under any variance, exemption or code interpretation. What to say: Submit a request for a zoning determination or schedule a pre-application meeting with Planning staff. State that the concept is a bar with live entertainment occupying 24,138 square feet on the first and second stories at 429 Castro Street, and that Planning Code Section 715 appears to prohibit uses of 4,000 square feet or more. Ask in writing: (1) whether the 4,000 square-foot cap is absolute, (2) whether any exemption or variance path exists, and (3) whether intensifying the existing nonconforming nighttime entertainment use on the second story is permitted under Section 186.1 given that new nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted. Request a written response before filing any application or paying any fee.
outcomes.note: The record confirms the district and Section 715 exist but does not state the 4,000 square-foot prohibition, Section 186.1, or any rules about nighttime entertainment uses.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms in writing that a path exists, form the legal entity, obtain the EIN, and register the business with the City. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70) and obtain the federal Employer Identification Number online from the IRS (same day, free). Then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number, required for all other City permits. Also file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, and publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks. The BAN, entity documents and FBN statement are prerequisites for the CUA application, the ABC license, and the health and building permits.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for the bar use and intensification of nighttime entertainment, if Planning's written determination in Step 1 confirms a path exists. What to say: Submit the CUA application to SF Planning with the project description, site plans, a community outreach summary, and the BAN. Frame the concept as a bar with live entertainment accessory to the bar, closing by midnight or 1 a.m., consistent with the 2012 approval of a place of entertainment accessory to a bar at 4141-4149 18th Street. Emphasize that the Castro Theatre is a neighborhood landmark, that the concept preserves the building's entertainment character, and that operating hours will respect residential neighbors. Expect neighborhood notification under Section 311, a Planning Commission hearing, and a 30-day appeal period.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the Place of Entertainment permit with the SF Entertainment Commission after or in parallel with the CUA filing, but do not schedule the Entertainment Commission hearing until the CUA is approved. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility and obtain the application packet. Submit the POE application online with the BAN, a copy of the lease or title, floor plans showing the performance area, a security plan, and a community outreach summary. Post a yellow notice at the premises for 30 days and conduct neighbor outreach. The Commission will refer the application to Police, Planning, DBI, Public Health, and Fire for review. At the hearing, present an acoustic study showing sound levels will not exceed residential noise limits, commit to hiring security staff during hours, and offer to close entertainment by midnight.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Decide the alcohol program (beer and wine or full liquor) and engage an ABC license broker if purchasing a Type 47 or 48 quota license, or apply for a non-quota Type 41 or 42 if serving beer and wine only. What to say: If the concept will serve beer and wine only, apply for ABC Type 41 or Type 42. If the concept will serve full liquor, purchase an existing Type 47 or Type 48 license on the open market through a broker; San Francisco licenses cost roughly $100,000 to $450,000. Before applying to ABC, obtain the California seller's permit from CDTFA. ABC will post a 30-day public notice at the premises. If the census tract shows undue concentration, the city or Planning must provide a Public Convenience or Necessity finding before ABC will issue; start the PCN request as soon as the ABC application is filed.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the building permit application to SF Department of Building Inspection with stamped architectural plans for tenant improvements and change of use, after the CUA is approved. What to say: Hire a licensed architect to prepare a plan set showing the bar layout, plumbing for sinks and bar equipment, mechanical for HVAC, electrical for lighting and amplified sound systems, accessible restrooms, and exit paths. DBI will route the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm the permit matches the CUA approval. If the space is for 50 or more people, obtain a Fire Department place of assembly permit showing occupancy load, exit signage, and any required hood suppression. Schedule DBI inspections for rough framing, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and final, and coordinate the final DBI inspection with the final DPH inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the health permit to operate with SF Department of Public Health after the building permit is approved and construction is at least 80 percent complete. What to say: Submit the health permit application online with the BAN, Location ID, federal tax ID, and a menu or description of beverages to be served. DPH will route the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm the use matches the CUA. Schedule a pre-opening inspection at 80 percent construction complete and a final inspection before opening. Have a certified food safety manager on staff and all food handlers with California Food Handler Cards before the final inspection. The permit to operate is issued after the final inspection passes.
outcomes.note: The record discusses business registration certificates, not health permits or DPH procedures.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for playing recorded music and hosting live performances, and ensure all alcohol servers complete RBS training before opening. What to say: Apply online for ASCAP and BMI blanket licenses at least two weeks before opening; the licenses are effective immediately and are required by federal copyright law for any public performance of music. Register each alcohol server and manager on the ABC RBS Portal, complete an approved RBS course, and pass the exam; the certification is valid for three years and must be on file at the premises for ABC inspections. Obtain workers' compensation insurance before the first employee starts and register as an employer with CA EDD within 15 days of paying wages.
